key_insight: Real patient-chatbot interactions are highly diverse, and this diversity can materially change LLM triage outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Healthcare conversational AI should be evaluated and designed for varied patient emotions, styles, and strategies—not just idealized cooperative users—to avoid biased or unsafe deployment.
method: Analyzed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations to characterize variation in clinical content, emotion, strategy, and style.
Built a patient simulator that models these four dimensions separately.
Tested realism with 15 human graders and assessed urgency prediction across 1,164 clinician-graded cases using five patient personae and four LLMs.
evidence_signal: The simulator was nearly indistinguishable from real conversations in a Turing-inspired test, and human graders identified real vs simulated chats with only 55% accuracy.
watch_item: A simulator that performs well in realism tests may still miss rare, high-risk, or culturally specific communication patterns that affect clinical safety and equity.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
